title: DNN-Assisted Deterministic Policy Learning for Adaptive IRS-NOMA-OWC Networks
summary: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has been considered a promising technology in optical wireless communication (OWC) networks due to its potential to overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) blockage issue and enhance coverage. In this paper, a dynamic IRS-assisted indoor non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-OWC network is modeled, and an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the sum rate subject to the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of multiple mobile users, by jointly optimizing the power allocation and the IRS mirror orientations, from which the user's decoding order is induced rather than being fixed. Since the problem is non-convex and the channel conditions vary with user mobility, conventional optimization methods may incur considerable computational overhead. Therefore, a two-stage deep neural network-deep reinforcement learning (DNN-DRL) framework is proposed. In the first stage, the DNN estimates the user's positions and orientations in real time, removing the need for perfect knowledge of the user state. In the second stage, a deterministic policy gradient (DPG)-based DRL algorithm uses these estimates to jointly optimize the power allocation and IRS mirror orientations, with the decoding order updated according to the resulting effective channel gains. The results show that the proposed framework approaches the performance upper bounds and outperforms standard DRL algorithms, conventional optimization methods, and deployments without IRS in terms of sum rate and fairness, while achieving faster convergence. Furthermore, online adaptation of the decoding order maintains higher QoS satisfaction than a fixed decoding order, particularly under high user mobility.

title: On Pareto-Optimal Estimation-Information Limits-Achieving Distributions for Integrated Sensing and Communications
summary: ISAC systems enable simultaneous data transmission and environmental sensing using a common waveform. Characterizing their fundamental estimation-information performance limits is of core interest in information theory. In this paper, the achievable data rate for communications and the Miller-Chang-type CRB on sensing distortion are adopted as ISAC performance metrics, both of which are functionals of the ISAC waveform distribution. Our aim is to characterize the optimal input distributions across the entire CRB-rate Pareto boundary, corresponding to different sensing-communication tradeoff preferences. Three types of power constraint on input waveform are considered, namely, i) general power (GP), ii) maximum amplitude (MA), and iii) constant modulus (CM) constraints. Under these constraints, Pareto-optimal input distributions are shown to exhibit a common structural property: the directional component is uniformly distributed over the complex unit sphere; the power distribution is discrete (excluding the communication-optimal point under GP, where it follows a Gamma distribution induced by Gaussian inputs). We further investigate and characterize their Pareto-optimal sensing-communication preference dependent support structures. Finally, numerical algorithms are developed under GP and MA to trace their Pareto boundaries and determine corresponding optimal power distributions based on their respective support characteristics. From both analytical and numerical results, we conclude sensing prefers deterministic power while communication benefits from a richer distribution of power levels, thereby revealing the sensing-communication waveform uncertainty tradeoff in the fundamental power domain.

title: Hybrid-Field Interference Suppression for Low-Complexity Uplink Channel Estimation
summary: Uplink channel estimation can be severely degraded by hybrid-field interference, where strong near-field intra-site interference is coupled with far-field inter-site interference. Although a joint near-/far-field dictionary can capture this interference structure, it requires dense angle--distance matching that may incur high complexity and performance degradation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid-field interference suppression framework for uplink channel estimation. First, we formulate a hybrid-field interference model and analyze its sparse reconstruction. Then, to avoid exhaustive near-field dictionary matching, we propose a low-complexity interference-parameter estimation method based on the angle--domain diffusion pattern of the dominant interference. Using the estimated parameters, the proposed parametric interference-nulling orthogonal matching pursuit (PIN-OMP) algorithm suppresses the dominant interference components and reconstructs the desired uplink channel from the interference-suppressed observation. Furthermore, a physical critical-distance bound is derived to characterize the feasible distance-inversion region, and a conditional hybrid Cram'er--Rao bound (HCRB) is established to quantify the desired channel reconstruction limit under a reconstructed interference basis. Finally, numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model
summary: Laboratory testing guides clinical diagnosis but requires blood sampling and processing. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is fast and noninvasive and may carry information about laboratory abnormalities, yet most AI-ECG models target one test at a time using 12-lead recordings. We conducted an exploratory ECG laboratory-wide association study (ECG-LabWAS), fine-tuning an ECG foundation model pretrained on 10.8 million ECGs to screen 50 laboratory tests from single-lead waveforms alone. The model was developed in an emergency-department cohort (MC-MED; 31,826 patients) and applied unchanged to an independent hospital cohort (MIMIC-IV; 115,921 patients). Of 89 abnormality directions (low or high values of each test), 33 met the same screening criteria in both cohorts. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the two cohorts were 0.841 and 0.838 for elevated NT-proBNP, 0.769 and 0.740 for elevated cardiac troponin, 0.755 and 0.731 for elevated creatinine, and 0.713 and 0.710 for low potassium. Discrimination changed little when the ECG--laboratory matching window was widened from $\pm$1 to $\pm$24 hours. Model predictions reproduced the co-occurrence of observed abnormalities but were about twice as tightly coupled, largely along one shared component consistent with overall illness severity; low potassium, elevated NT-proBNP and troponin, and markers of renal function retained discrimination beyond that of correlated tests. In exploratory analyses, ECG-assisted versions of the modified Glasgow Prognostic Score and the systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria were associated with in-hospital and one-year mortality. These results identify which laboratory abnormalities warrant analyte-specific study with single-lead ECG.

title: User-Irrepressible Sequences for Multiple-Packet Reception
summary: This paper studies deterministic transmission schemes based on protocol sequences for slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception (MPR) channels without feedback or synchronization of sequence phases. Each user schedules its transmissions according to a preassigned periodic binary sequence. A sequence set has the user-irrepressible property with MPR capability $\gamma$ ($\gamma$-UI) if every user is guaranteed at least one successful transmission per period, regardless of the relative cyclic shifts. We propose a unified explicit construction based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) for arbitrary MPR capability $\gamma\geq 2$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified CRT-based construction framework for $\gamma$-UI sequences over this full range, without requiring conflict-avoiding codes with prescribed parameters. We establish the $\gamma$-UI property through bounds on pairwise Hamming cross-correlations and show that suitably selected subsets support one additional active user without increasing the sequence length. We also derive exact average individual delay expressions over all possible cyclic shifts and extend the delay analysis to $\gamma$-UI sequence sets obtained from conflict-avoiding codes.

title: PepDeTech: Anonymous Occupancy Monitoring on a Battery-Powered 2.3k-Zone dToF LiDAR Node with On-Chip Processing and Bluetooth LE Reporting
summary: As populations grow, society is increasingly required to shift towards systems of shared resources, which allow space, energy and time to be optimised. Facilitating this transition depends on data: how many people are present, when and where. From such information, schedules can be organised more efficiently and resources allocated where they matter. At the same time, privacy concerns and energy consumption limit deployment: cameras are frequently unacceptable, while simpler sensors miss people and cannot provide the full picture. This paper presents PepDeTech, a compact, battery-powered occupancy node that combines a 54 x 42-zone direct Time-of-Flight (dToF) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) (VL53L9CX) with a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) System on Chip (SoC). Three deterministic algorithms, background subtraction, motion history and a track lifecycle, run on-chip and count the people simultaneously, providing real-time occupancy monitoring. No trained model is involved, and setup takes less than a minute. Over three scenarios, background subtraction reaches a per-frame +-1-person accuracy of 83.6 % (mean absolute error (MAE) 0.70 persons), tested with up to five people present. At a 30 s interval the node draws only 3.1 mW, lasting 60 d on a 1200 mA h cell. Several weeks of deployment on a single charge make the node usable as a survey instrument for facility management: a room can be characterised for a measurement campaign without cabling, network provisioning or a camera, and the resulting occupancy record is what ventilation, lighting, cleaning and space-allocation decisions are argued from, ultimately resulting in more efficient resource allocation.

title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
summary: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.

title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
summary: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.

title: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications
summary: We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_\lambda(x)=x^{3q-1}+\lambda x^{2q}+\lambda x^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_\lambda$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $\lambda=0$, or $\lambda\ne0$ and $X^3+X+\lambda^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $\lambda$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_\lambda$ parameterized by $P_\lambda(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $\lambda$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.

title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.

title: Geometrical Estimation of Electromagnetic Degrees of Freedom in Reflecting Environments
summary: The number of spatial degrees of freedom (NDoF) of electromagnetic communication channels in reflecting environments is investigated using a full-vector formulation based on dyadic Green's functions and equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents. The channel correlation eigenproblem characterizes the electromagnetic communication modes and their coupling strengths, while the leading-order NDoF is estimated geometrically from the receiver-accessible phase space volume in the electrically large regime. By combining two geometrical projection Jacobians, the phase space volume is related to the mutual shadow area, establishing the equivalence between the two geometrical NDoF formulations and yielding a two-polarization estimate equal to twice the mutual shadow area divided by the squared wavelength. The free-space mutual shadow formulation is extended to perfect electric conductor (PEC) reflecting environments through image construction and phase space ray tracing, accounting for specular reflections and geometrical visibility constraints. The formulation is validated against the eigenvalue spectra of full-vector electromagnetic channels involving planar PEC reflectors, a parabolic reflector, a parallel-plate waveguide, and a non-line-of-sight L-shaped corridor. The geometrical predictions agree with the observed spectral transitions across configurations involving multiple reflections, focusing, and blockage.

title: Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading
summary: A codeword spans a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks. The receiver knows the gains and the transmitter knows only their law. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, we require the decoding error probability to decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. When does outage predict the achievable rate? If block length grows faster than the number of antennas, outage gives the limiting optimal rate. If both grow to infinity at a fixed positive ratio of block length to array size, outage strictly overestimates the limiting rate. We determine the critical ratio above which positive rates are possible. For sufficiently large finite ratios, we find the exact limiting rate over all codes satisfying a total energy constraint on each codeword. The leading rate loss is inversely proportional to the ratio. Its coefficient depends on Gaussian channel dispersion at the most likely fade causing outage and on how quickly the outage rate decreases as the required error exponent increases. In the long-block limit, equal power loses rate on every window of three or more blocks under stationary first-order autoregressive fading with positive lag-one correlation. In a different three-block channel with identical marginal gains, tightening the reliability requirement first makes it optimal to leave the middle block unused and later to use it again.

title: $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
summary: We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.

title: A Dual-Mode Protocol for Space-Time-Coding Metasurfaces in OFDM ISAC Systems
summary: Existing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks assisted by space-time-coding metasurfaces (STCMs) rely on idealized surface models, which neglect the frequency-selective and angle-dependent response of the meta-atoms, and are typically limited to narrowband single-carrier communications. This paper addresses these limitations by developing a physics-based signal-processing framework for STCM-assisted ISAC systems employing wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms, which accounts also for beam squint effects across the STCM aperture. On this basis, we propose a dual-mode protocol, in which the STCM operates as a time-varying surface during a short acquisition phase and as a conventional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) during data transmission. In the acquisition phase, the angle of arrival (AoA) and the composite channel are jointly estimated by maximum likelihood from a single pilot OFDM symbol transmitted over a subset of active subcarriers, together with deliberately introduced virtual carriers; these estimates are then used to configure the RIS for data transmission. Numerical results validate the considered framework and quantify the gains achievable by the proposed dual-mode protocol.

title: A Spatial Clustering and Resource Allocation Approach for Critical Services in Massive MIMO-Enabled Cellular Networks
summary: In this work, we address the challenge of providing quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees for critical real-time services in cellular networks where both real-time and non-real-time applications must be supported. Leveraging the spatial multiplexing capabilities of Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology, we propose a joint clustering and resource allocation framework that limits network interference and enhances the ability to meet the QoS requirements of real-time services while still serving other applications. Our approach begins by clustering active users according to the direction of their channel vectors. Specifically, a downlink probing strategy is employed to group users whose channels lie in the same direction. Channel estimation and the derivation of the corresponding signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) are then performed based on this clustering. Subsequently, we formulate a resource allocation optimization problem across the user groups to satisfy the required QoS for critical real-time services while accommodating the remaining users. We rigorously prove that, in general, finding the global optimum of the resource allocation problem is NP-hard, and for a special case of the formulated problem, we establish a polynomial-time solvable algorithm based on linear programming. We then propose a suboptimal solution for the general problem using a linear relaxation technique. Simulation results are provided to confirm the effectiveness of our proposed approaches.

title: FR3-Band Capacitive-Piezoelectric Thin-Film LN Resonator for Heterogeneous Integration
summary: This letter presents a capacitively coupled piezoelectric lateral-field-excited bulk acoustic wave resonator (XBAR) in single-crystal lithium niobate (LN) for frequency range 3 (FR3, 7.125-24.25 GHz). We develop a platform that simultaneously maintains high electromechanical efficiency (\(k_t^2\)) and quality factor (\(Q\)) while alleviating challenges associated with parasitic galvanic interconnections and is fit for heterogeneous integration above integrated circuits. A 100 nm air gap excites the second-order symmetric Lamb wave (S2) mode in a 500 nm thick periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) LN from a fused silica substrate via flip-chip bonding, yielding a resonance frequency (\(f_s\)) of 7.16 GHz with an extracted \(k_t^2\) of 12.25\% and \(Q\) of 100, facilitating a high \(Q\cdot k_t^2\cdot f_s\) product of 87.71. The results demonstrate strong piezoelectric transduction through a nanoscale air gap, supporting further development of the platform for heterogeneous integration of compact, low-loss microwave components.
